headline: Optical and Connectivity Names Spark a Broad Monday Rally as Chip-Equipment Makers Slide
body_html:
Stocks were firmly higher at midday Monday, with prices still moving and not final. Of the 666 names we track, 556 were rising and 107 were falling. The dominant theme was a surge in companies tied to optical networking and data-center connectivity.

Semiconductors led every sector on our table at 12.73, ahead of financials at 7.18, materials at 3.08 and industrials at 3.06. Homebuilders barely moved, at 0.12. The standout movers were Applied Optoelectronics, up 25.83%, Credo Technology, up 25.61%, and Coherent, up 23.36%. Bloom Energy, MaxLinear and Vicor each gained more than 21%.

The rally was not uniform. Chip-equipment makers listed abroad sold off sharply: Lasertec fell 12.23%, DISCO 12.00% and Tokyo Electron 8.28%. CrowdStrike also lost 7.60%. Into the close, watch whether the connectivity gains hold, whether the equipment weakness spreads, and how traders handle the Iran headlines. Tuesday's session will show whether the move has follow-through.

briefs.headline: Optical Names Dominate the Leaderboard
briefs.body: Applied Optoelectronics and Coherent both climbed more than 23% in the session so far, joined by Credo Technology at the top of the board. The cluster points to heavy demand for networking and connectivity hardware. Intraday moves of this size can reverse, so the close matters.

briefs.headline: Chip-Equipment Makers Take the Brunt
briefs.body: Lasertec and DISCO each fell about 12%, while Tokyo Electron lost 8.28% and VAT Group 7.79%. BE Semiconductor Industries slipped 4.66%. The group moved against the strength in other chip stocks, making it the most notable pocket of weakness in the market today.

briefs.headline: Volatility Gauge Flashes a Contrarian Signal
briefs.body: A widely watched measure of market anxiety has reportedly given a buy signal, a pattern some traders read as a sign that fear has peaked. Broad participation today, with far more stocks rising than falling, fits that story. One session proves little, though.

briefs.headline: Gulf Markets Close Higher on Diplomacy
briefs.body: Most Gulf bourses finished higher, helped by optimism over diplomatic progress in the region. The move offered a supportive backdrop for global risk appetite. Tension over a US naval blockade, which Iran vows to resist, keeps the picture fragile.

briefs.headline: Iran Vows Resistance to US Naval Blockade
briefs.body: Tehran says it will use every available tool to confront the American naval blockade. The rhetoric adds a geopolitical risk factor for energy traders into the afternoon. Energy was among the stronger sectors on our table today, up 2.78.

briefs.headline: Diesel Tightness Clouds the Oil Recovery
briefs.body: Commentary this week argues that oil's rebound after the Iran conflict hides a stubborn shortage of diesel. Separately, China's electric-truck boom is lifting demand for lithium. Together they show how fuel and battery-metal markets are being pulled in different directions.
